title: How much does a trip to Italy cost?
summary: See how much a trip to Italy costs from five regions, with flights, hotels, trains and a budget range for each traveller. Compare.
body_markdown:
We've all heard about the Colosseum, the Leaning Tower of Pisa and the Trevi Fountain, but what I loved most about Italy was everything in between.


I spent three months there, and even the simplest moments felt like scenes from a historical film. I could spend hours wandering through old streets, admiring the architecture or sitting in a piazza with a coffee, just watching life go by. It's the perfect place to embrace *il dolce far niente* , the Italian art of doing nothing and enjoying every minute of it. And, of course, eating more pasta and gelato than I'd like to admit.


One thing I learnt during those months is that you don't need a huge budget to enjoy Italy. But you do need to plan a little, especially if you're hoping to visit several cities.


Trips to Italy can be surprisingly affordable or quite expensive, depending on where you're coming from, when you visit and how you travel. A week in Rome, Florence and Venice, for example, will cost more than staying in one smaller town.


A one-week trip to Italy costs roughly $1,500 to $3,500 per person. Budget travellers spend around $1,500 to $2,200, mid-range $2,500 to $3,500, and luxury $6,000 or more. Flights vary most by origin, while trains between cities and summer hotel rates shape the daily budget.


So, how much should you actually save for your Italy trip? Let's break down the costs, from flights and accommodation to food, trains and those extra gelatos you'll inevitably want.


## How much does a trip to Italy cost? Budget range overview


The cost of a trip to Italy depends on a few things: where you're flying from, how long you're staying, the time of year and your travel style.


For a seven-day holiday, here's what you can expect to spend per person, including an estimated return flight from the US.


Travel style Estimated cost for 7 days


Budget $1,500–$2,200


Mid-range $2,500–$3,500


Luxury $6,000+


‍


These are planning estimates, not fixed prices. Summer is generally the most expensive time to visit, particularly in popular destinations such as Rome, Florence, Venice and the Amalfi Coast.


Your itinerary also makes a difference. Visiting three cities in one week means more train tickets and potentially higher accommodation costs. Staying longer in one place can help you save.


And if you're still deciding where to go in Europe, you might also want to compare[how much a trip to Greece costs](https://grey.co/blog/trip-to-greece-cost) . Once you've settled on Italy, our guide on[what to pack for a Europe trip](https://grey.co/blog/what-to-pack-for-a-europe-trip) can help you prepare.


## How much does a trip to Italy cost from the USA?


If you're travelling from the US, flights will probably be one of your biggest expenses.


Return economy tickets to Rome or Milan typically cost around $600 to $1,200, although prices depend on your departure city, season and booking dates.


Flying from New York or Boston can be cheaper than departing from the West Coast, especially when direct flights are available.


Here's an estimated budget for seven days:


Expense Estimated cost


Return flight $600–$1,200


Accommodation $350–$1,050


Food and drinks $210–$420


Transport $100–$250


Attractions $80–$200


Total $1,340–$3,120


‍


For a comfortable trip, budgeting around $2,500 to $3,000 per person is a reasonable starting point.


If you're planning to visit Rome, Florence and Venice, consider arriving in Rome and flying home from Venice, or vice versa. This can save you the time and cost of travelling back to your arrival city.


## How much does a trip to Italy cost from North America?


For travellers coming from Canada or Mexico, flights are also likely to take up a significant part of the budget.


From major Canadian cities, return flights to Italy can cost approximately $700 to $1,300 USD. Toronto and Montreal often have more direct connections, while flights from western Canada may involve longer journeys.


From Mexico, prices vary considerably depending on your departure city and available connections.


Here's a general seven-day budget in USD:


Expense Estimated cost


Return flight $700–$1,300


Accommodation $350–$1,050


Food and drinks $210–$420


Transport and attractions $180–$450


Total $1,440–$3,220


‍


If you have flexible travel dates, compare flights to both Rome and Milan. Sometimes, arriving in a different city can make a noticeable difference to the overall cost.


## How much does a trip to Italy cost from Europe?


Travelling to Italy from another European country is usually much more affordable, particularly if you're flexible with your dates.


Low-cost airlines connect Italy with cities such as London, Paris, Barcelona, Madrid and Berlin. Depending on your route, return flights can cost around €80 to €300.


Just remember that the cheapest fares often don't include checked luggage.


For seven days in Italy, you could spend:


Expense Estimated cost


Return flight €80–€300


Accommodation €280–€840


Food and drinks €175–€350


Transport and attractions €130–€350


Total €665–€1,840


‍


If you're travelling from a neighbouring country, trains and buses are also worth considering.


And if you only have a few days, I'd recommend choosing one region rather than trying to squeeze in every major city. Spending four days in Florence and exploring Tuscany, for example, can be a lovely way to experience Italy without constantly packing your bags.


## How much does a trip to Italy cost from Africa?


The cost of travelling to Italy from Africa varies quite a bit depending on where you're departing from.


Travellers from North African countries such as Morocco, Tunisia and Egypt may find shorter and more affordable flights. From countries such as Nigeria, Kenya or South Africa, journeys are generally longer and may require connections.


Return flights can cost approximately $400 to $900 on selected routes, although some departures can be considerably more expensive.


Here's an estimated seven-day budget in USD:


Expense Estimated cost


Return flight $400–$900


Accommodation $350–$1,050


Food and drinks $210–$420


Transport and attractions $180–$450


Total $1,140–$2,820


‍


Depending on your nationality and residence status, you may also need a Schengen visa. Remember to include the application fee, travel insurance and any additional processing charges in your budget.


## How much does a trip to Italy cost from South America?


If you're travelling from South America, getting to Italy will probably be the most expensive part of your holiday.


Return economy flights from major cities such as São Paulo, Rio de Janeiro, Buenos Aires and Bogotá can cost around $1,000 to $1,800, depending on the route and season.


Some cities have direct flights to Italy, while others require a connection.


Here's what a seven-day trip might cost:


Expense Estimated cost


Return flight $1,000–$1,800


Accommodation $350–$1,050


Food and drinks $210–$420


Transport and attractions $180–$450


Total $1,740–$3,720


‍


Since flights are relatively expensive, I'd consider staying for at least 10 to 14 days if your schedule and budget allow.


You'll spend more overall, but you'll have more time to explore and won't feel as though you've crossed the Atlantic just to rush through three cities.


## Trip to Italy cost breakdown: Flights, hotels, trains and food


Now that we've covered the cost of getting to Italy, let's look at what you'll actually spend once you're there.


The nice thing about Italy is that you have plenty of choices. You can stay in a luxury hotel, eat at expensive restaurants and book private tours, but you can also have an incredible trip with simple accommodation, local food and public transport.


Here's a breakdown of typical expenses:


Expense Budget option Mid-range option


Accommodation per night €40–€80 €100–€180


Breakfast €3–€7 €8–€15


Lunch €10–€18 €20–€35


Dinner €15–€25 €30–€55


Local transport per day €3–€8 €8–€15


Museum or attraction €10–€20 €20–€35


Rome to Florence train €20–€45 €45–€75


Florence to Venice train €20–€45 €45–€70


‍


These are approximate planning ranges. Accommodation prices depend on the type of room or bed, and train fares vary by departure time and booking date.


### Accommodation: Location matters more than you think


Rome, Florence and Venice are among the more expensive places to stay, especially during the summer.


But you don't necessarily need to stay right next to the main attractions. Choosing accommodation a little further from the historic centre, but close to public transport, can save you quite a bit.


In Venice, for example, staying in Mestre on the mainland is often cheaper than booking a hotel on the islands. Just remember to account for the time and cost of travelling into Venice.


Smaller cities such as Bologna, Padua and Perugia are also worth considering if you'd like to experience a different side of Italy.


### Food: Good meals don't have to be expensive


If there's one thing I wouldn't worry too much about in Italy, it's finding good food.


You can have a delicious plate of pasta, pizza or a panino without spending a fortune. And honestly, some of the simplest meals are the ones I remember most.


A quick breakfast at a local café might cost €3 to €7, while a casual lunch can be around €10 to €18.


For dinner, expect to spend approximately €15 to €25 at an affordable restaurant.


One thing to keep in mind is the coperto, a cover charge some restaurants add to your bill. It's usually a few euros per person and should be listed on the menu.


And a small tip from my time there: having your coffee standing at the counter is often cheaper than sitting at a table, especially in tourist areas.


### Trains: The best way to travel between Italian cities


If you're visiting several cities, trains are probably going to be your best friend.


Italy has an extensive railway network, including high-speed services connecting major destinations such as Rome, Florence, Milan, Naples and Venice.


For example, the high-speed train from Rome to Florence can take around 90 minutes, making it much easier than dealing with airports.


There are two main high-speed operators: Trenitalia and Italo. You can compare fares on their websites and often find better prices by booking early.


Regional trains are usually cheaper and work well for shorter journeys, particularly if you're exploring smaller towns.


The[official Italian tourism website](https://www.italia.it/en/italy/practical-information/how-to-travel-around-italy) also has useful information about getting around the country.


### Attractions: You don't need to pay for everything


Italy is practically an open-air museum.


Of course, places such as the Colosseum, Vatican Museums and Uffizi Gallery are worth considering, but some of the best experiences are completely free.


Walking through Rome, admiring Florence's architecture or wandering around Venice can easily fill an afternoon.


For paid attractions, budget approximately €10 to €35 per visit, although guided tours and special experiences can cost more.


I'd recommend choosing a few attractions you really want to see and leaving some free time to explore without a strict itinerary.

## Frequently asked questions about the cost of a trip to Italy


### How much does a trip to Italy cost for one week?


A one-week trip to Italy generally costs around $1,500 to $3,500 per person, including flights, accommodation, food, transport and activities.


Budget travellers may spend less by staying in hostels, eating at casual restaurants and travelling outside peak season. Luxury holidays can easily exceed $6,000 per person.


### Is Italy expensive for tourists?


Italy can be expensive in popular destinations such as Venice, Rome, Florence and the Amalfi Coast, particularly during summer.


However, it's possible to travel affordably by visiting smaller cities, using public transport and choosing local restaurants.


Your accommodation and travel dates will usually have the biggest impact on your budget.


### How much does a 10-day trip to Italy cost?


A 10-day trip to Italy can cost approximately $2,000 to $4,500 per person, including an estimated return flight from the US.


Budget travellers might spend around $2,000 to $2,800, while mid-range travellers could spend $3,000 to $4,500.


The total depends on your itinerary, travel season and accommodation choices.


### What is the cheapest month to visit Italy?


January, February and November are often among the cheapest months to visit major Italian cities, excluding holidays and special events.


Hotels can be more affordable, and popular attractions are generally less crowded.


If you'd prefer warmer weather, April, May, late September and October can offer a good balance, although prices may be higher.


### How much spending money do I need for seven days in Italy?


Excluding flights and accommodation, budget around €40 to €70 per day for an affordable trip or €80 to €150 for a more comfortable experience.


That's approximately €280 to €490 for a budget week or €560 to €1,050 for a mid-range trip.


You don't need to carry everything in cash, as cards are widely accepted across Italy.


### Is it cheaper to visit Rome, Florence or Venice?


Rome and Florence generally offer more accommodation options across different budgets, while staying in central Venice can be particularly expensive.


However, prices depend on the season and neighbourhood.


If you're trying to save, consider staying outside the historic centre or visiting nearby towns.


### How can I save money on a trip to Italy?


Travelling outside the summer season, booking trains and accommodation early, and spending more time in fewer cities can help reduce costs.


Eating at local restaurants, using public transport and combining paid attractions with free activities also makes a difference.


And if you're paying in a currency other than euros, remember to compare exchange rates and card fees before travelling.


## Make the most of your Italy trip


Three months in Italy taught me that some of the best travel experiences don't require much money. Sometimes, all you need is a beautiful town to explore, a good meal and enough time to enjoy where you are.


Planning your budget means you can spend less time worrying about expenses and more time enjoying everything Italy has to offer.
